newsitem.title: ANGOLA: ANGOLA-CHRISTOPHER PRESSES FOR RAPID PEACE AGREEMENT.
newsitem.headline: ANGOLA-CHRISTOPHER PRESSES FOR RAPID PEACE AGREEMENT.

text.p: LUANDA, Oct 14 (Reuter) U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Monday directed a senior aide to meet Jonas Savimbi to press the UNITA chief to stop delaying implementation of the Angolan peace agreement.
Christopher, wrapping up a five-nation African tour, wanted to meet Savimbi in Luanda to deliver the U.S. message on Angolan's threatened peace process.

But Savimbi, who once depended on Washington and white South Africa to finance his guerrilla war against the then-Marxist Angolan government, turned down the request on grounds he could be in danger if he came to the capital.
Christopher rejected Savimbi's suggestion the two men meet in another country or at the UNITA leader's base camp because it "would send the wrong signal," U.S. officials said.
Instead he decided to sent George Moose, assistant secretary of state for African affairs, senior U.S. officials said.

"We are obviously concerned, as are others, at the delays in the process and the impact those delays would have on the confidence in the future of the implementation of the peace process," said Moose, who is to meet Savimbi at his bush stronghold of Pailundo in the central highlands.
"That is the concern I will be registering in my direct conversation with Dr Savimbi," he told reporters who flew with Christopher from Capetown, South Africa.
On arrival, Christopher went immediately into talks with Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
U.N. peace troops are to be withdrawn from Angola beginning next February when a 1994 peace agreement between the government and UNITA is supposed to be fully in effect.
Although both parties have at various times dragged their feet on the accord, the United States and the United Nations blamed UNITA this time.
